clue.text: Married but misbehaving, with view to getting lost here?

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not keep their proper places, so the words married but are rearranged

parts.note: an angle is a point of view or perspective

explanation.surface: A spouse strays during a marriage, with an eye to disappearing somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges MARRIED BUT into BERMUDATRI; 'with view' then adds ANGLE. 'to' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is the stretch of Atlantic Ocean notorious for ships and planes said to vanish there.

clue.text: Without religion? Possibly idealistic without it

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way, so idealistic is rearranged
without asks for the letters of the word it to be left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A query whether being free of faith might count as idealistic, provided you drop something.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: shuffle IDEALISTIC, having first removed I and T, both signalled by 'without it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made secular has been removed from church control, so it is left free of religion.

clue.text: Top notch communist broadcast

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, read as the letters AI
a communist is a Red

explanation.surface: A first-rate leftist goes on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, 'top notch', is written with the figure 1 standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean transmitted on radio or television, as with a programme put out on air.

clue.text: Slipshod of the Spanish or French to intervene in stroke

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the article goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to stroke is to caress
the definite article is le in French (and el in Spanish, which also fits reversed letters); either way it gives LE

explanation.surface: A sloppy piece of foreign grammar meddles in a swimming stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests swimming or illness, but it is a gentle touch. Spanish EL and French LE are both 'the'; the grid wants LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is done without attention or care, which is what the answer describes.

clue.text: Maintain important-sounding little dog?

indicators.note: important-sounding asks for a word meaning important said aloud, spelt another way

parts.note: key means important, as in a key witness
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A tiny dog with a grand-sounding air is to be kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY said aloud is written KEE; 'little dog' supplies PUP, and together they say 'key pup'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep up a garden or a standard is to sustain it and stop it slipping.

clue.text: Make laws member's passed on

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member, and the 's is read as is
late means dead, someone who has passed on

explanation.surface: A member of parliament has passed new legislation into law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member's' is read as LEG IS; 'passed on' is a euphemism for died, so LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to enact statutes, the work of a parliament.

clue.text: Home papers rejected by court charge

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters for papers run the other way

parts.note: ID stands for identity papers

explanation.surface: Home Office documents get thrown out by a court hearing a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ID into DI. 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict someone is to formally accuse them of a crime, as a verb meaning charge.

clue.text: Snake catches Native American airing out before it can climb walls

indicators.note: a snake that catches something holds it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: a viper is a venomous snake

indicators.note: out signals the letters of airing are put out of order

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A snake seizes an indigenous man who is getting fresh air before scaling a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airing' looks like part of the snake scene but is anagram fodder for 'out'; the Cree people sit beside it, and 'catches' puts both inside the snake. 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine famous for covering house walls and turning red in autumn.

clue.text: Get rid of command, having lost time after time

indicators.note: after places the shortened command behind the second time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: having lost means one letter of the command has gone missing

parts.note: to dictate is to command

explanation.surface: Abolish an order, losing time again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' appears twice and does two jobs: once as the single letter that 'having lost' removes, once as a period, which 'after' puts first.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate something is to destroy it completely, wiping it out.

clue.text: Every third Etonian studying shows dissatisfaction

indicators.note: every third letter is taken, starting from the first, through the two words

explanation.surface: One in three boys from Eton is visibly fed up with his studies.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13 of ETONIAN STUDYING give the answer; 'shows' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom, a state of discontent with one's lot.

clue.text: The mace deployed as a weapon

indicators.note: deployed means set out in a new arrangement, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A spiked club is brought into battle as an arm.
explanation.walkthrough: A mace is itself a weapon, a tempting decoy, but 'deployed' rearranges THE MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade, used for cutting vegetation and as a weapon.

clue.text: Soft assonance heard in preparation

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: heard means a word is said aloud and then spelt differently

parts.note: rhyming is the matching of sounds, a near-relation of assonance

explanation.surface: A gentle chime of vowel sounds is heard while getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' asks for RHYMING spoken, which is spelt RIMING; P for soft goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Priming is the preparatory step, as with a first coat on wood or a pump made ready.

clue.text: Find record at an end

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished

explanation.surface: Someone finds an old record when everything is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come upon or find it, often for the first time.

clue.text: Neat, polite and not totally Italian

indicators.note: each of the three words is not taken in full: its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A description of someone tidy and courteous, though not entirely Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut the last letter off each word: NEA(T), POLIT(E), AN(D).
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan describes someone or something from Naples, which makes it Italian.

clue.text: Working blouse on either sex is doing very well

parts.note: on means operating or working, as with a machine
a top is a blouse or shirt
F or M stand for female or male, and either sex is read as F OR M

explanation.surface: A work shirt fit for anyone is performing splendidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either sex' reads as F OR M, female or male. 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on top form is an idiom for being at one's best and performing excellently.

clue.text: Starting telly is depressing: it normally gives sad news

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Television is gloomy because it usually brings bad reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'telly is depressing it normally gives sad' spell the answer, leaving 'news' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is a slightly old-fashioned word for reports or information received.

clue.text: Something from the florist, the ultimate in tulip arrangement for auntie

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so the final letter of the flower word is taken
an arrangement puts things in a new order, here the letters of auntie

explanation.surface: A florist offers a tulip arrangement as a present for an aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' seems to belong to the flower shop, but it signals the rearranging of the relative's word; 'the ultimate in' supplies the last letter of the flower. 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A petunia is a popular bedding flower, the kind sold in a flower shop.

clue.text: Travel essential for Dad's hobby

parts.note: pa is dad, and pa's gives PAS
a sport is a pastime or hobby

explanation.surface: Father's favourite pastime is a must-have for trips abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the identity document needed for international travel.

clue.text: Unbelievably bad bile, out in colour

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are in poor order and must be rearranged
out means the letters of bile are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Bile that is incredibly bad is coming out tinted.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: take B, I, L, E out of UNBELIEVABLY, as 'bile, out' says, and rearrange the rest. 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy blue is a dark shade, named for naval uniforms.

clue.text: Strange locations featuring intro to Cockney Rebel

indicators.note: featuring means including, so one letter goes into the rearranged word
strange suggests the letters of locations are oddly arranged
the intro is the opening, so the first letter of Cockney is taken

explanation.surface: Odd places host the opening of a song by the band Cockney Rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges LOCATIONS into ICONOLAST, and 'featuring' puts C inside it. Cockney Rebel was a 1970s British band.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast attacks established beliefs, a rebel against convention.

clue.text: With 11, 12, 13 or 8 films as once directed

indicators.note: directed, a film-making word here, means the letters are set out in new order

explanation.surface: A list of a heist film series' sequels, as once directed.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are not cross-references: Ocean's Eleven, Twelve, Thirteen and Eight are the films. 'directed' rearranges AS ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The heist films Ocean's Eleven, Twelve, Thirteen and Eight complete the title when a number follows the word.

clue.text: Without covers, all told, vital novel

indicators.note: without covers means each word loses its outer letters, leaving only the inside

explanation.surface: Stripped of its jacket, the whole book is still a crucial novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The insides of aLl, tOLd and vITAl give the answer, Nabokov's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the 1955 novel by Vladimir Nabokov.

clue.text: See 13
Fresh air in vacated tenement property

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the emptied word
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of tenement remain
fresh suggests a new version, so the letters of air are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clean air in an empty block of flats is a selling point for the property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties TENEMENT to TT; 'Fresh' rearranges AIR into RAI, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a characteristic, the sense of property as a quality something has.

clue.text: They say massage before flu treatment is essential

indicators.note: they say marks a word said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to knead is to massage

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of flu are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a rub-down before treating flu is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' works only on the massage word, which sounds like a want; 'treatment' is the anagram signal for the illness. 'before' and 'is' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needful is necessary, required or indispensable.

clue.text: Drop Arab leader's story

indicators.note: the 's says the answer is possessed by, held within, the words drop Arab leader

explanation.surface: An Arab leader is being dropped, according to a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside dROP ARAB LEader; the possessive 's, 'has', signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a simple story told to teach a moral lesson.

clue.text: Articles from Le Monde and the Guardian secure coverage of both sides of the moon

indicators.note: the two side letters secure coverage around the articles, so those go inside

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both sides
un is the French indefinite article, as printed in the paper Le Monde
a is the English indefinite article, as printed in The Guardian

explanation.surface: Two newspapers, French and British, both cover the moon from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Monde is a French daily, so its article is UN; the Guardian, English, gives A. 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar is the adjective meaning relating to the moon, from Latin luna.

clue.text: Turning prude, I tut on seeing this

definitions.text: Turning prude, I tut on seeing this

indicators.note: turning means the letters are rotated into another order

explanation.surface: Someone becomes prim and clicks their tongue at what they see.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: depravity is what would make one tut disapprovingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is wickedness or depravity, the sort of conduct a prude disapproves of.
